observations.observation: An orientation wrapper passed @{u} to PowerShell without quoting it, so PowerShell parsed a hashtable literal and stopped before Git execution.
observations.correction: The explicit quoted ref and later literal local, tracking, ls-remote, and GitHub head checks passed.

observations.observation: A retrieval-report probe guessed artifacts/evaluations/runs/baseline-0031-retrieval-control.json, which does not exist.
observations.correction: The frozen comparison contract supplied the exact control and candidate paths; both reports contain 136 Boolean gates and matching gate-key inventories.

observations.observation: The retrieval selection verifier derives coverage_and_adversarial_stage_contracts_pass with all(...) over filtered Boolean gates. A synthetic mutation that removed the complete coverage and retrieval-stage inventory could make that single derived check vacuously true.
observations.current_exposure: nonblocking for BASELINE-0031 because the exact public 136-gate control and excluded candidate reports, receipts, comparison, manifest, premerge audit, reviewed Git head, and selected v3 default remain bound; v4 already fails five gates and is not promoted
observations.attempted_correction: A narrow explicit inventory guard and mutation test passed 94 of 94 tests.
observations.release_boundary: The correction correctly failed the frozen 153-file manifest on the changed verifier, so it was reverted byte-exactly instead of rewriting the verified package and image lineage.
observations.next_checkpoint_requirement: Make absent or substituted selection-gate inventories fail closed in the next checkpoint before evaluating another retrieval candidate.

observations.observation: A 40-validator wrapper run while the review mutation existed stopped at verify_baseline.py because verify_manifest.py reported exactly scripts/verify_retrieval_tier_cap_result.py changed.
observations.correction: The two-file review mutation was reverted byte-exactly; the active manifest and comparison validator then passed.

observations.observation: A manual validator inventory mistakenly included the legacy verify_baseline.py orchestration command, which can create and promote a new evaluation after its regression phase.
observations.containment: The exact Python and wrapper processes were stopped during the regression phase before evaluation creation or promotion; Git status remained clean and no candidate evidence changed.
observations.correction: The corrected set excludes side-effecting verify_baseline.py and includes immutable report/trace verification instead.

observations.observation: The first corrected trace command omitted PYTHONPATH and the second guessed a non-existent source-attempt path.
observations.correction: The exact source report and trace under artifacts/evaluations/runs passed with PYTHONPATH bound to src; the complete corrected set passed 40 of 40.

observations.observation: PowerShell wrapped GitHub array responses as nested arrays during one pagination probe, and one later anonymous request hit a transient DNS failure.
observations.correction: Curl with retry and direct array handling proved all 112 local and GitHub PR paths equal; connected GitHub state remained clean and mergeable at the exact head.

observations.observation: The first public-audit verification wrapper used an invalid Where-Object expression and stopped before producing a result.
observations.correction: The exact successor verified the audit bytes, Git blob, length, SHA-256, branch head, and PR head.

observations.observation: The first fresh-clone validator wrapper required dist/runbook-sentinel-0.0.31.pyz before rebuilding it, so the package verifier correctly reported the ignored release artifact missing.
observations.correction: All 40 contract and project validators passed without asserting a not-yet-built archive; two subsequent builds reproduced and independently validated the selected archive exactly.

observations.observation: A package-contract probe requested a nonexistent top-level artifact property.
observations.correction: The exact path is candidate.artifact; two builds and the canonical checksum passed.

observations.observation: Long PowerShell wrappers for merged-main evaluation and tracked structured parsing outlived the first output-yield window, so their session identifiers were not retained by the wrapper.
observations.containment: Evaluation files completed normally and were independently re-read and verified; the slower read-only parse wrapper was stopped and replaced with a faster no-write parser.
observations.correction: Exact report, trace, JSON, and JSONL results are recorded in merged-main-baseline-0031.json.

observations.observation: Two credential-scan attempts placed a leading-hyphen pattern before the ripgrep option terminator and then placed globs after the terminator.
observations.correction: The exact successor reports zero token material, zero complete private-key blocks, twenty-six definition or historical literal matches, and zero unresolved credential finding.

observations.observation: Both Windows PowerShell Edge launches emitted the existing fallback task-provider diagnostic after writing the requested PNG.
observations.correction: Both commands exited zero; source and package PNGs are complete 1440 by 1000 frames and passed original-detail inspection.

observations.observation: The first milestone-validation wrapper named nonexistent optional profile .codex/project.json and therefore returned invalid before evaluating the contract.
observations.correction: The milestone contract declares no project profile reference; the exact successor invokes the governing validator on contracts/milestone-0031.json without inventing one.

observations.observation: A generic forty-script wrapper passed thirty-three validators but omitted three source import bindings and four required lifecycle flags, so seven validators correctly failed instead of attesting the wrong phase.
observations.correction: The exact successor binds PYTHONPATH to src and supplies the current implementation, excluded-candidate result, and canonical container-result requirements declared by each lifecycle validator.

observations.observation: The first phase-correct successor supplied retrieval-observability implementation-only mode without its companion require-implementation flag; that validator rejected the incomplete phase declaration after thirty-nine other passes.
observations.correction: The exact successor supplies both flags, matching the implemented current lifecycle without changing any project byte other than this retained process receipt.

observations.observation: The first publication wrapper applied array indexing directly to a native-command expression, yielding the first character 1 instead of the complete remote Git hash and stopping before push.
observations.containment: Remote main remained exact at 1b0ad59a59f566c8d10e7069d3ed8ffdb974f7fd and no network mutation occurred.
observations.correction: The exact successor stores the ls-remote output before splitting and comparing the complete hash.

observations.observation: The first anonymous GitHub reconciliation wrapper did not brace the tree hash before the query delimiter, so PowerShell misparsed the URL and GitHub returned 404 before raw-path comparison.
observations.containment: The wrapper was read-only; public and local repository state did not change.
observations.correction: The exact successor braces the hash in the recursive-tree URL and repeats all ref, tree, and raw-byte comparisons.

observations.observation: The first resume-orientation wrapper used the older BASELINE-0030 rollout-summary filename after the current memory registry had advanced to the BASELINE-0031 pause summary, so the wrapper stopped before reading any skill instruction.
observations.containment: The lookup was read-only and did not change repository or external state.
observations.correction: The exact successor used the current registry path, read the BASELINE-0031 pause summary, and then read every required governing skill and release/reconciliation reference completely.

observations.observation: The first artifact and Docker inventory wrapper placed a pipeline immediately after a foreach block, which PowerShell rejected as an empty pipeline element before executing any read.
observations.containment: The wrapper failed at parse time and changed neither repository nor external state.
observations.correction: The exact successor assigns the foreach results to an array before serializing and separates artifact, Docker, and source-reference probes.

observations.observation: The first exact-identity inventory guessed three nonexistent contracts paths for the retrieval cap, package, and container records.
observations.containment: The read-only probe reported the paths missing and did not use them as negative product evidence.
observations.correction: Repository inventory identifies the exact paths as eval/retrieval-tier-cap-contract.json, eval/package-contract-0031.json, and eval/container-contract-0031-v11.json before hashing or audit use.

observations.observation: The Docker 29.4.3 client was installed but the desktop-linux daemon pipe was absent at final-audit orientation, so live image inventory and renewed scan commands could not run.
observations.containment: No container command mutated state; the exact August 18 candidate-bound container-runtime-v11 receipts remain retained but are not misrepresented as a fresh August 22 observation.
observations.correction: Restart only the authorized local Docker verifier environment, then recheck exact image custody and rerun the point-in-time scan before relying on a current container claim.

observations.observation: A read-only milestone search passed contracts/schema* literally to ripgrep on Windows, which rejected the invalid path after returning the useful explicit contract matches.
observations.containment: The search changed no repository or external state and its partial output was not used to infer schema validity.
observations.correction: Use explicit directories plus ripgrep -g filters and inspect the governed milestone validator before changing lifecycle fields.

observations.observation: The first audit-template read guessed a nonexistent templates directory after the exact skill inventory had already shown the file under assets.
observations.containment: The failed read was local and read-only; no audit was drafted from an unknown template.
observations.correction: Read the exact enumerated assets/release-audit-report.json and the independent evaluator before authoring the blocked audit.

observations.observation: The first renewed Docker Scout command targeted an unowned shorthand tag, attempted a registry fallback, and failed to pull before producing SARIF.
observations.containment: No image was pulled, exported, pushed, published, or redistributed; the failed command provided no positive or negative security evidence.
observations.correction: Inventory the exact local tags first and use the local:// prefix; the successor scanned image ID sha256:3736d003e1c57fc30bf831145c151d2457593d5fc0596a16ad387b7db07a72c1 without registry fallback.

observations.observation: A combined anonymous GitHub inventory correctly reconciled all four main refs and v0.0.31 absence but returned a null latest-release projection from a PowerShell array/filter expression.
observations.containment: The null was treated as incomplete wrapper output, not as release absence or project evidence.
observations.correction: Query the official releases/latest endpoint directly; it reports public non-draft non-prerelease v0.0.30 published at 2026-08-17T23:19:14Z.

observations.observation: A read-only evidence search passed artifacts/verification/baseline-0031* literally to ripgrep on Windows, which rejected the invalid path after the exact merged-main regression summary had already been read.
observations.containment: The partial search output was not used as a complete validator inventory and no repository or external state changed.
observations.correction: Use the explicit artifacts/verification directory with -g baseline-0031*.json and retain the side-effecting verify_baseline.py exclusion.

observations.observation: The first exact-command recovery reader used File.OpenText on the active Codex rollout and Windows denied the default exclusive-share request.
observations.containment: The read-only lookup produced no command inventory and changed no repository, product, or external state.
observations.correction: Open the active audit log explicitly with FileShare.ReadWrite; the successor recovered the exact side-effect-free 40-validator command set, which then passed unchanged.

observations.observation: The first resume probe passed HEAD^{tree} through the PowerShell command wrapper without a quoting-safe form, so the wrapper mangled the revision argument and Git rejected that tree query while the independent HEAD and remote-main reads still completed.
observations.containment: The probe was read-only; the rejected tree query was not used as reconciliation evidence and repository, release, tag, image, and external state did not change.
observations.correction: Use git show -s --format=%T HEAD; the successor returned tree 956f42afea4ec56c00b524230cb5cdb5df03b3c4 and reconfirmed a clean worktree at commit fd01cb566241f342094c17ba5949222ad8556ddf.

observations.observation: The first anonymous post-publication check interpolated a tree hash immediately before ?recursive=1, so PowerShell treated the query suffix as part of the variable expression and GitHub returned 404 before a complete reconciliation result existed.
observations.containment: The failed check was anonymous and read-only; no partial response was used as public verification evidence and repository, release, tag, image, and external state did not change.
observations.correction: Build the tree endpoint by explicit string concatenation; the successor reconciled local, tracking, ls-remote, and anonymous refs at 492baf3c389994c596501894a7457bf7c0ded22d, matched tree 3216361f9b80ca817531cd13cb86b7d2e8852e11, confirmed an untruncated 1,450-entry tree, and matched both published evidence files byte for byte.

observations.observation: The first immediate four-ref check after publishing OBS-030 returned false even though the exact commit tree and raw failure receipt already matched the public commit surface.
observations.containment: The false aggregate was treated as a transient incomplete reconciliation result, not as proof of ref divergence or release readiness; no state-changing action followed it.
observations.correction: Read each ref independently after propagation; local HEAD, explicit tracking, ls-remote main, and anonymous GitHub main all converged on 6e21908f4917a2432f5c9e631813cb471ca4f4d4.
